refs: BRV 2024 replacement market: 47.5M tyres (cars, vans, trucks), 95% consumer, season mix and channel shares, as reported by AUTOHAUS and meinauto.de, March 2025
BRV managing director, around 2018: fleet and leasing is about 17.5% of car replacement
Roland Berger, 2018 (context only): about 50 German tyre wholesalers, top 7 hold about 75%
ETRMA publishes members' (pool) replacement sales; Germany-level pool and non-pool figures were not found publicly

Research file (Germany consumer replacement tyre distribution 2024): BRV 2024 channel shares of 71% specialist and independent, just under 20% dealers, 3.5% Fachmärkte and 5.5% B2C online (as reported by Reifenpresse and AUTOHAUS); the manufacturer-direct versus wholesale split, non-pool imports, export balance and private versus commercial splits are model estimates and should be treated as indicative.

ETRMA Europool Germany car-tyre sell-in of 46.8M (+7%), cited in the research file via Pirelli Germany statutory reporting, versus BRV sell-out of about 41.0M: the gap is why industry sell-in should not be expected to equal consumer sell-out. Not independently verified here.

UN Comtrade / WITS 2024, HS 401110: Germany gross imports 87.8M and exports 53.1M passenger tyres. These show Germany is a large cross-border hub but cannot be used directly for the wholesale import and export boxes.
Only the net is pinned down by the data: wholesale exports net of non-pool imports come to about 6.4M. Any change to the import assumption moves the export balance one for one.
Wholesale infrastructure examples (research file): Best4Tires serves more than 33,000 dealers and workshops with more than 20 manufacturers; Reifen Müller stocks about 500,000 tyres.
